objective: Minimize transmitted bytes with exact reconstruction. Endpoint compute and elapsed time are measured tradeoffs, not first-delivery latency gates.

local_tcp_demo.workload: 1 MiB deterministic xorshift bytes, exact repeat, then XOR 0xa5 over offsets [524288,524320)
local_tcp_demo.timing_interpretation: Recorded single-run elapsed time is diagnostic. Concurrent local checks and excluded setup preclude latency distribution or WAN speed claims. Mutation was slower than cold transfer on loopback.

random_16m.scope: real TCP loopback; 16 MiB random cold zstd/raw fallback and exact repeat; includes private cache restart
random_16m.input_storage: public random input and recovered output retained locally under local/qualification-16m; source digest identifies this exact trial

included: all protocol headers, manifests, requests and commit responses
cold cache seed reported separately and in cumulative demo total
excluded: authenticated transport overhead (transport is not authenticated)
input file reads, selected base-graph preparation and connection establishment from elapsed_micros
accounting.comparison: Warm and cold entries use the same local protocol wrapper and durable endpoint. Conventional CAS, rsync/VCDIFF, independently secured raw transfer and shaped WAN baselines were not run.

limits_and_gaps: Loopback-only CLI uses fixed trusted context/authority for public or synthetic data; it provides no peer authentication or encryption.
Current sender is synchronous. Missing-record repair is tested; request pipelining is not implemented.
DAG uses fixed 32-byte leaves. Prefix insertion and scattered edits may lose reuse; no general compression or speedup claim.
The 64 MiB protocol ceiling is not large-object or DAG-cache qualification. The initial functional demonstration reached 16 MiB; random cold data may exceed DAG warming budgets.
Cache/resident budgets require one Endpoint per process. Returned caller-owned buffers are outside endpoint quota. No peak-RSS qualification was performed.

Publication verifies exact bytes then syncs and atomically renames within a private owned cache. Partial in-flight transfers are volatile; restart recovery covers complete publications. Physical power-loss storage behavior was not qualified.
MVM mailbox and FlowMux adapters, three-peer recovery, real WAN impairment, 30 paired trials and conventional baseline comparisons remain future work.
FIPS 140-3 module validation and CUI deployment controls are not established by this implementation.
Research mechanisms remain in the audit claim ledger; symbolic discovery, physical time synchronization and routing/compression hypotheses are not promoted to measured network claims.
